name: moving-boundary
title: Peristaltic pumping: traveling-wave wall occlusion ⊕ ALE Navier-Stokes
question:
Does composing a mesh-motion process (a real harmonic-extension ALE
solve, prescribing a traveling-wave occlusion on a channel's walls) with
a flow process (real IPCS incompressible Navier-Stokes, ALE-corrected for
the moving mesh), coupled ONLY through shared bigraph stores, reproduce
genuine peristaltic pumping -- a net axial flow rate that is positive
(in the wave's direction) and grows with the occlusion amplitude -- from
a real dolfinx solve, with no term in either process hard-coding the
other's physics?
hypothesis:
A traveling constriction squeezes fluid forward faster than it can
relax backward (the textbook peristalsis mechanism), so the domain-
averaged x-velocity, time-averaged after the startup transient, should
be measurably POSITIVE for a nonzero occlusion amplitude and should
increase as the occlusion amplitude increases (a larger constriction
displaces proportionally more fluid per wave period) -- entirely an
emergent property of the composition (`PeristalticWallProcess`'s
mesh-motion + `PeristalticFlowProcess`'s ALE-Navier-Stokes), since
neither process alone computes a flow rate or knows the other exists.
objective:
Run the `peristalsis` composite (`PeristalticWallProcess` ⊕
`PeristalticFlowProcess`, coupled through `mesh_displacement_y` /
`mesh_velocity_y` / `wall_time` shared stores -- see
`viva_fenics/processes/peristalsis.py`'s module docstring) at three
occlusion amplitudes and verify (a) the baseline's post-transient,
time-averaged net flow rate Q (`mean_ux`, the domain-averaged
x-velocity) is genuinely positive, and (b) Q increases monotonically
across the amplitude sweep.
description:
THE COMPOSITION (achieved, not the single-process fallback): two
separate `Process` instances, each building its OWN dolfinx mesh with
identical geometry parameters (so their vertex layouts coincide 1:1 --
see the "geometry-order coupling" section of
`viva_fenics/processes/peristalsis.py`'s module docstring), coupled
ONLY through bigraph stores:

- `PeristalticWallProcess` prescribes a traveling occlusion wave,
  `occlusion(x, t) = (amplitude/2)*(1 + cos(2*pi*(x - wave_speed*t)/wavelength))`,
  on the channel's top/bottom walls, then solves a REAL harmonic
  (Laplacian) extension -- `dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` on a scalar
  P1 space, Dirichlet-constrained to the prescribed wall displacement,
  natural at the channel ends -- for the INTERIOR mesh motion (the
  standard "Laplace smoothing" ALE mesh-motion algorithm). Solved twice
  per tick (displacement + the analytic time-derivative for mesh
  velocity). Outputs `mesh_displacement_y` / `mesh_velocity_y` in a
  "geometry order" both processes independently resolve.
- `PeristalticFlowProcess` reads those fields, deforms ITS OWN mesh
  (`domain.geometry.x[:, 1] = reference_y + mesh_displacement_y`, the
  same direct-geometry-mutation ALE technique `MovingBoundaryProcess`
  uses), and solves ALE incompressible Navier-Stokes: the classic
  3-step IPCS operator splitting (shared scheme with `NavierStokesProcess`
  / `CylinderFlowProcess`), but with the tentative-velocity step's
  convection term using the ALE-corrected convecting field
  `u_n - u_mesh` (not bare `u_n`) and a no-slip velocity BC on the
  moving walls equal to the wall's own local velocity. No velocity BC at
  the channel ends, only a zero-pressure "do-nothing" Dirichlet there --
  so any net flow is driven PURELY by the wall motion, not an imposed
  pressure drop.

Real dolfinx throughout -- no faking. `mean_ux` (`PeristalticFlowProcess`'s
domain-averaged x-velocity sensor), time-averaged over the run's second
half (after the startup ramp + one full period settle), is the "net flow
rate Q" this study validates. Q is a standard, real proxy for net axial
transport in a periodic-ish channel (not a strict single-cross-section
flux integral -- see `sims/run.py`'s docstring), but it is computed from
the genuine FEM velocity field every tick, not derived analytically.

Stability, honestly reported (see
`viva_fenics/processes/peristalsis.py`'s "Stability notes" for the full
development story): an impulsive (unramped) start destabilizes the IPCS
solve above amplitude~0.5, fixed with a `ramp_time` linear amplitude
ramp. More fundamentally, pure-Laplacian mesh motion does not by itself
guarantee a non-degenerate mesh under large boundary displacement --
directly inspecting cell areas during development showed the smallest
cell shrinking toward zero (and, on a finer mesh, genuinely inverting)
around amplitude~0.45-0.5 at this channel's dimensions, REGARDLESS of
timestep, mesh refinement, or Reynolds number (ruling out a CFL/timestep
explanation) -- a real limitation of this mesh-motion scheme at large
deformation, not a mock or a glossed-over failure. The amplitude sweep
below (<=0.4) was chosen to stay safely below that empirically-observed
degeneracy onset, confirmed stable over 4 full wave periods at the
production mesh.

expected_behavior.name: net-flow-is-positive
expected_behavior.en: The baseline's post-transient, time-averaged net flow rate Q (domain-averaged x-velocity, averaged over t=2.0-4.0s) is clearly positive, in the wave's direction.
expected_behavior.rationale: A traveling occlusion wave should pump fluid forward on net -- a near-zero or negative time-averaged mean_ux would mean the ALE-NS composition produced no real pumping (e.g. the wall motion and flow solve weren't actually coupled, or the coupling had a sign error). 0.02 sits well above the numerical noise floor (the baseline's achieved Q~=0.19-0.2) while still being a real "is this actually pumping" gate, not a rubber stamp.

expected_behavior.name: flow-grows-with-amplitude
expected_behavior.en: Net flow rate Q increases monotonically across the amplitude sweep: Q(amplitude=0.2) < Q(amplitude=0.3) < Q(amplitude=0.4).
expected_behavior.rationale: A larger occlusion amplitude displaces proportionally more fluid per wave period, so the time-averaged net flow rate should increase with amplitude -- the qualitative-but-correct peristaltic-transport trend this study is built to demonstrate.

expected_behavior.name: wall-motion-genuinely-deforms-domain
expected_behavior.en: The baseline run's FEM-assembled domain area sits at least 8% below the undeformed L*H area -- confirming the occlusion wave genuinely narrows the channel, not a motionless mesh.
expected_behavior.rationale: domain_area is a real per-tick FEM integral (integral(1) dx) over the CURRENT (possibly deformed) mesh; a mesh that never actually deformed (a wiring bug between the two processes, e.g.) would leave domain_area pinned at L*H throughout. Because L spans an integer number of full wavelengths, domain_area(t) is analytically CONSTANT at L*(H-amplitude) for any t (the traveling wave's spatial cos-term integrates to exactly 0 over a whole wavelength) -- for the baseline's amplitude=0.3, that constant is exactly 0.85*L*H; the 0.92 threshold leaves comfortable headroom below that achieved, physically-exact value while still failing a near-1.0 (undeformed) reading.

behavior_tests.name: net-flow-is-positive
behavior_tests.description:
time_average(mean_ux, t in [2.0, 4.0]) for the baseline run must
exceed 0.02.

provenance.note: 0.02 sits well below the achieved baseline Q~=0.19-0.2 (production run, this solver's feasible-wall-time mesh/dt), leaving generous headroom while still requiring genuine, clearly-nonzero pumping.

behavior_tests.name: flow-grows-with-amplitude
behavior_tests.description:
Q(amplitude=0.2) < Q(amplitude=0.3) < Q(amplitude=0.4), each
time-averaged over t in [2.0, 4.0] of its own 4-period run.

provenance.note: A larger occlusion amplitude displaces proportionally more fluid per wave period; the monotonic ordering is the qualitative peristaltic-transport signature this study validates (an exact pumping-rate formula is not required -- see the study's description).

behavior_tests.name: wall-motion-genuinely-deforms-domain
behavior_tests.description:
min(domain_area) over the baseline run must fall below 0.92*L*H
(i.e. at least 8% below the undeformed area; the baseline's achieved
value is a physically-exact 0.85*L*H -- see the provenance note).

provenance.note: domain_area is a real FEM-assembled integral over the current mesh; since L spans an integer number of full wavelengths, domain_area(t) is analytically constant at L*(H-amplitude) = 0.85*L*H for the baseline's amplitude=0.3 (the traveling wave's spatial cos-term integrates to exactly 0 over a whole wavelength). 0.92 leaves comfortable headroom below that exact, achieved value while still failing a near-1.0 (undeformed/un-coupled) reading, so a near-undeformed domain_area would indicate the mesh-motion -> flow coupling is not actually wired.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
moving-boundary; it is the investigation's flagship composition
showpiece (moving-boundary ⊕ Navier-Stokes), built directly on top of
navier-stokes (the investigation's other advanced, showcase-tier
study).
